content.text:
My child who tears up at the thought of kindergarten

With the first day approaching, seeing your child cry "I don't want to go" or "I want to stay with Mommy" weighs on a parent's heart too. That feeling of feet frozen in front of the yellow bus—it's completely understandable.

Fearing a new environment isn't your child being difficult; it's a natural feeling anyone has in the face of the unfamiliar. At this stage, a heads-up like "it's going to be okay" is far more powerful than any pushing.

Curious about the kindergarten adjustment storybook? Take a look at its lessons alongside the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the story too. Read it together with your child and talk it over.
content.caption: Fearing a new environment is a natural feeling anyone has.

content.alt: 41. Nervous at First, but Soon Friends! - Why adjusting to a new environment matters
content.text:
Why adjusting to a new environment matters

Starting kindergarten is the first bit of 'little social life' a child ever experiences. Get through this first hurdle well, and your child feels less anxious and grows braver in front of new places and new people.

On the other hand, when first-day fears go uncomforted, they can turn into a refusal to go at all. What matters is for your child to feel firsthand that 'even when you're nervous, it soon turns out okay.'
content.caption: Get through the first-day jitters well, and your child grows braver.

content.alt: 41. Nervous at First, but Soon Friends! - The first day of kindergarten, Bori's story
content.text:
The first day of kindergarten, Bori's story

In 『Nervous at First, but Soon Friends!』, Bori crouches in a corner of the unfamiliar classroom with tears welling up. Just then, the rabbit teacher holds out a hand: "Everyone's a little nervous at first. Would you like to hold my hand?"

Holding the teacher's hand, Bori is joined by Hori and Toto, who come over to play. Bori works up the courage, and before long is romping and giggling with new friends. At pickup time, Bori beams and shouts, "Mom! I made a friend! I want to come again tomorrow!" Along with Bori, your child experiences a day where fear turns into fun.
content.caption: The once-unfamiliar classroom became an exciting playground.

content.alt: 41. Nervous at First, but Soon Friends! - Getting ready for school together at home
content.text:
Getting ready for school together at home

Starting a few days before, read this book together and give a heads-up: "It's okay to be nervous at first—you'll make friends soon." A story your child can anticipate greatly eases their anxiety.

When your child is scared, rather than asking "What's so scary?", read the feeling with "You're nervous because it's unfamiliar." At drop-off, make a clear promise—"I'll be back to get you for sure"—say a bright goodbye, and part ways short and sweet; that reassures your child far more.
content.caption: A clear promise and a short goodbye give your child reassurance.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q. What should I do when my child doesn't want to go to kindergarten?

A. Reassure them through the story that even if they're nervous at first, they'll make friends soon. Saying a bright goodbye and promising when you'll meet again puts your child's heart at ease.

Q. Can a kindergarten adjustment storybook help?

A. Watching the main character settle into an unfamiliar place, your child gains courage too. A kindergarten adjustment storybook gently eases the fear of a new environment.

Q. How do I help a child who cries at every drop-off?

A. Embrace the crying heart first, say a short, bright goodbye, and hand them over with trust. Talking together after pickup about the fun parts of the day gradually makes kindergarten a comfortable place.
